title: Philippines eyes over $2-billion US military loan after Trump visit
summary: The same information sheet describes the package as a "historic" deal that would "support over 7,000 American jobs" and advance the US' "first arms transfer strategy, all while protecting returns for…

blocks.text: US President Donald Trump arrives in Manila on Tuesday, November 17, for the 49th ASEAN Summit.

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines is eyeing a loan of more than $2 billion (over P127 billion) from the United States to buy defense and security equipment from American suppliers, plus $400 million (around P25 billion) in military financing for deterrence operations in the South China Sea, the White House announced on Thursday, November 19.
The amounts were listed in a White House information sheet released after US President Donald Trump wrapped up a two-day visit to Manila.

Under the "historic foreign military financing loan package," the Philippine government would be using the loan to procure defense and security equipment from US suppliers that would "provide the Philippines with critical defense and security capabilities," the government release read.

The same information sheet describes the package as a "historic" deal that would "support over 7,000 American jobs" and advance the US' "first arms transfer strategy, all while protecting returns for the American taxpayer."

On top of this, the US is also providing the Philippines $400 million in foreign military financing "to expand its operational reach and deterrence capabilities in the South China Sea." This includes procuring long-range fires, command and control systems, critical infrastructure, and drones, according to the information sheet.
Up to $500 million a year in military financing grants had been previously authorized by the US Congress for the Philippines from 2026 to 2030.

The White House also announced two separate agreements between the Philippines' Department of National Defense (DND) and US firms it did not name, which will provide the DND with artificial intelligence-enabled mission support and defense infrastructure.
The US is the only country with which the Philippines has a mutual defense treaty, which covers armed attacks on either country’s armed forces in the South China Sea, including coast guard ships.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio reaffirmed Washington’s commitment to the treaty as recently as July.

The announcement comes after President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said at the close of the 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila on Wednesday, November 18, that negotiations for the South China Sea code of conduct, a framework of rules to manage disputes in the area, were “85% to 90%” complete.
Negotiations will continue under Singapore, which takes over the ASEAN chairship in 2027.
Beyond defense, Marcos and Trump had also discussed economic cooperation, including what the US president claimed was Washington's "biggest trade deal" ever.
A later release by the Presidential Communications Office said both sides "have reached an understanding" on energy and food security.
